evidence.detail: Exact v308 rs/z/a stores exactly two long values: a start timestamp populated from System.currentTimeMillis() and a constructor-supplied duration.
Its start method records the current time, active-state compares elapsed milliseconds against duration, and remaining-time returns max-like zero-or-duration-minus-elapsed behavior.
R250 CooldownManager constructs rs/z/a(duration), starts it immediately, and stores it as the keyed cooldown timer for login and tray-notification throttling.

candidates.note: DurationCooldownTimer is a conservative descriptive recovery for the concrete fixed-duration implementation used exclusively by CooldownManager. It does not claim a verbatim original developer identifier. Confidence 0.998.

evidence.detail: Exact v308 rs/z/b is abstract and defines the three operations implemented by rs/z/a: start(), active-state boolean, and remaining milliseconds.
R250 CooldownManager stores Map<String, rs.z.b> and invokes the active-state and remaining-time operations through this abstract type.
The only exact-v308 subclass/reference family is rs/z/a, the fixed-duration currentTimeMillis-backed implementation used by CooldownManager.

candidates.note: CooldownTimer is a conservative descriptive recovery for the abstract timer contract owned by CooldownManager. It does not claim a verbatim original developer identifier. Confidence 0.997.
